title: US-Iran war and shipping attacks around the Strait of Hormuz
what_happened: Military action in the Middle East that began in early March 2026 cut shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and drove oil sharply higher. Brent averaged $124 in October and fell below $100 in early November. New attacks on vessels on 2026-11-24 were reported but are not yet confirmed here.
how_it_reaches_markets: Oil prices feed inflation and therefore rate expectations; shipping disruption; risk-off moves on escalation.

sourced_facts.text: EIA, 2026-03-10: Brent 'has risen sharply following the onset of military action in the Middle East' and 'settled at $94 per barrel on March 9'; shipments through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen
Brent spot averaged $124 a barrel in October 2026 and fell below $100 on 2026-11-04; EIA forecasts about $100 for November and December (Short-Term Energy Outlook, released 2026-11-10)

EIA estimates Middle East production shut-ins at 2.5 million barrels a day in October, down from 10.9 million at the peak in May, and expects exports from Iran to remain constrained through the forecast period

resolved_when_all: A ceasefire or agreement is publicly announced by both governments
No reported attack on commercial shipping in or around the Strait of Hormuz for 60 consecutive days
Brent settles below 80 dollars for 20 consecutive trading days
worsened_when_any: Strait of Hormuz closed to commercial traffic

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: Announcements of talks without a ceasefire

counter_view.note: The strongest reason this card's reading may be wrong. AFMX's own judgment, using the facts listed on the card.
counter_view.text: Supply is coming back: production shut in has fallen from 10.9 to 2.5 million barrels a day and Brent from an October average of $124 to under $100. The $80 line is our own choice. If the economy has adjusted to oil near $100, the risk could fade well before our conditions say so.
